sources.title: Library of Congress: Country Profile, Thailand (July 2007)
sources.note: Direct PDF. Historical Background pp.4 to 7: constitutional change, wartime alliance and resistance, postwar government, military rule and political openings. Obsolete current-officeholder information is excluded.

sources.title: Thai Parliament: Guide to the National Assembly
sources.note: Direct English guide, published 2008, printed pages 1 to 2: 24 June 1932 Khana Ratsadon revolution and the change from absolute monarchy. Imported feature dates/bounds are independently decoded in identities.json; the guide does not certify atlas geometry.

sources.title: ASEAN: The Founding of ASEAN
sources.note: Institutional indexed history, opening paragraphs: Bangkok Declaration, five founders, 8 August 1967. Promotional assessments of institutional success are excluded.

sources.title: House of Commons Library: Thailand, political developments 2023 to 2024
sources.note: Direct institutional briefing, 18 November 2024. Sections May 2023 general election, Move Forward leader blocked, and party dissolved. Historical coup dates 2006 and 2014, not a claim about current officeholders.

sources.title: OHCHR: Thailand decision to end prosecution of civilians in military courts
sources.note: Original indexed release, 13 September 2016. Civilian military-court prosecutions introduced after the 2014 coup; decision ending new prosecutions welcomed.

sources.title: Bank of Thailand: Lessons learnt from the Asian Financial Crisis
sources.note: Direct central-bank retrospective: fixed exchange regime, capital inflows and property bubble, speculation, float on 2 July 1997 and regional crisis.

sources.title: World Bank: Thailand country overview
sources.note: Direct current overview checked September 2026, About section. Use historical national poverty-line figures for 2000 and 2021, not the different PPP poverty series. Agriculture-to-industry transformation and regional inequality. Legacy /en/country/thailand/overview treated as same work.

sources.title: World Bank: Thailand Economic Monitor, February 2026
sources.note: Original indexed key findings, Advanced Green Manufacturing section: 25 percent of GDP, 16 percent of employment, more than 6.2 million workers. These are report-time figures, not projections of future success.

sources.title: UNESCO: Songkran in Thailand, traditional Thai New Year festival
sources.note: Original indexed nomination description, inscribed 2023. Mid-April after rice harvest, family reunions, respect for elders, water, games, feasting and transmission. Query suffix ?RL=01719 is same work.

sources.title: UNESCO: Nora, dance drama in southern Thailand
sources.note: Full original indexed description checked; direct extraction returned only challenge wrapper. Costumes, long metallic fingernails, bird-like wings, oboe/percussion, master training and regional dialects.

sources.title: UNESCO: Tomyum Kung
sources.note: Original indexed 2024 nomination description: prawn soup, herbs, riverside communities, family transmission. Folk wellness beliefs not presented as demonstrated medical effects.

sources.title: Thai Government Public Relations Department: UNESCO recognition of Tomyum Kung (6 December 2024)
sources.note: Direct Thai HTML: title and first paragraph spell ต้มยำกุ้ง and give romanization Tomyum Kung. Second paragraph explains components ต้ม ยำ กุ้ง. Translation supported by UNESCO nomination. Digital 2024 witness, no invented ancient inscription.

sources.title: UNICEF: Bridge to a Brighter Tomorrow, Patani Malay-Thai multilingual education
sources.note: Original indexed UNICEF account, 26 October 2024, describing research begun 2007. Pilot/comparison schools and phased language instruction. Group with 2018 Mahidol/UNICEF report and its country landing page as one work.

sources.title: UNICEF: Books and school uniforms used to be here
sources.note: Direct report, 27 November 2024: nine-year-old Abdulloh at Ban Talo Star School, Raman District, Yala; late-2023 floods, lost uniform and missed school. Named account, not a national rate.

sources.title: WHO: In Thailand, universal health care eases the impact of diabetes
sources.note: Direct report, 4 April 2016: 2002 financing change, local testing/referral, insulin and test-strip distinction; schoolchild Sip and dancer Kim. Historical account of care, not personal treatment instructions.

sources.title: WHO: Thailand village health volunteers during COVID-19
sources.note: Direct report, 28 August 2020: Somchai Chachumpa, Koo Bang Luang, meals and morning calls during quarantine; family records, dengue breeding containers and vaccination work.

sources.title: UNICEF: Bringing the gift of clean water to migrant children
sources.note: Direct/original indexed full article, 19 March 2024. Pyo Nyi Nyi, age 11; farm community after flight from Myanmar; mid-2023 hygiene kits, toilets, bathing stations, purifiers and maintenance training. Distinguish local account from national coverage.

sources.title: WHO: Thailand first country in Asia to eliminate mother-to-child transmission of HIV and syphilis
sources.note: Direct validation release, 7 June 2016. Validation of transmission-elimination targets, not eradication of HIV or syphilis from the country.

sources.title: Pisit Charoenwongsa and Chester Gorman: Ban Chiang, Expedition 18.4 (1976)
sources.note: Original indexed full primary excavation account. Uses only 1974/1975 fieldwork locations, team methods and observed objects. Early proposed bronze/iron dates and origin claims were subsequently contested and are deliberately excluded.

sources.title: OHCHR: Thailand marriage equality law takes effect
sources.note: Original indexed release dated 24 January 2025, statement 23 January. Effective 23 January 2025; marriage recognition and medical/property/inheritance/adoption implications.

scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

Imported border coordinates remain unchanged. Historical events and map coverage are distinguished in prose; see batchIdentityNotes for conflicts.

proposedOverrides.name: Thailand
proposedOverrides.summary: Modern Thailand: political change, public health, family traditions and a continuing state.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One modern country record only; no aliases or associations with earlier Siam, Ayutthaya or Rattanakosin cards.
batchIdentityNotes.mapCoverage: HB circa 1945 to open end; five decoded snapshots 1945,1960,1994,2000,2010 with nearly identical bounds 97.372 to 105.476 E and 5.531 to 20.458 N. Snapshot validity ends 2020; index open.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: 1932 constitutional revolution is prior context. Imported 1945 is not foundation. Six nonoverlapping exclusive intervals; last endpoint 2027 is an editorial viewing interval including 2026 dated evidence, not predicted state ending.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Exact ต้มยำกุ้ง and Tomyum Kung in Thai Government PRD 6 December 2024 article; English meaning from UNESCO 01879. Unicode text checked directly, no invented historical manuscript.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Modern national overview; refugee water, child illness and flood accounts are named local evidence. No timeless universal household custom or claim all residents share one language/religion. No current officeholder assertion. Earlier archaeological dates in 1976 report deliberately not reused.
